thread.title: Big Buys of BlackBerry, Intel, Qualcomm Stock

author: Ed Lin
title: Big Buys of BlackBerry, Intel, Qualcomm Stock
text:
Photo: Getty Images 
Toronto-Dominion Bank started out in 1855 as a humble single branch that served grain millers and merchants. Now TD Bank makes its bread through financial services world-wide. As of Oct. 31, the bank had assets of C$1.3 trillion. As of Dec. 31, it manages $31.1 billion in U.S.-traded equities.
TD Bank (ticker: TD) has expanded from its agricultural-servicing roots and has sown investments in technology. In January it acquired artificial intelligence (AI) startup Layer 6 of Toronto. The bank expects the deal to help it anticipate and meet customer needs.
Along those lines, we wonder if TD Bank consulted any form of AI in making some adjustments to its tech investments in the fourth quarter. There was a startlingly large purchase of BlackBerry (BB) shares, along with large purchases of Intel (INTC) and Qualcomm (QCOM) shares. TD Bank also saw fit to lop off more than a quarter of its investment in Micron Technology (MU).
BlackBerry was once shorthand for portable devices but now it remains fixed in memory as yet another company laid low by Apple ’s (AAPL) iPhone and apps. The mobile software and services company has fallen so far off the radar, many investors probably don’t even notice that BlackBerry changed its American stock listing to NYSE from Nasdaq in October. That’s a shame because BlackBerry had a cracking 2017 with shares up 62%--triple the gain of the Standard & Poor’s 500 Index. The company has been steering itself to the driverless-car sector . TD Bank more than quadrupled its holding in BlackBerry by buying over 1.5 million more shares in the fourth quarter, ending the year with just under 2 million shares. After recent market turmoil shares are essentially flat for 2018 in midday trading Friday.
Intel rose 31% in 2017, half of BlackBerry’s gain, but it was still enough to juice investors. TD Bank certainly wasn’t sour on Intel, as it bought 686,000 more shares of the chip giant in the fourth quarter, pushing holdings to 2.5 million shares. We’ve written earlier this month about how Intel could benefit from an iPhone rethink . TD Bank may be rethinking its Intel purchases--shares are down 7% so far in 2018.
Micron topped both BlackBerry and Intel by surging 88% in 2017, but like Intel it is down about 7% year-to-date. TD Bank sold 112,000 Micron shares in the fourth quarter, a period when the stock’s rise for the year stood at 127%; by the end of 2017, the bank’s investment stood at 308,000 shares.
TD Bank bulked up on Qualcomm in the fourth quarter, increasing its investment by 40% to 1.62 million shares. The wireless-chip maker is willing to meet Broadcom (AVGO), its would-be acquirer . Maybe Qualcomm is for sale at a higher price , but a richer valuation is a difficult thing to argue for as the market continues to twist .
TD Bank is the largest shareholder of TD Ameritrade (AMTD), which has responded to the recent market malaise . TD Ameritrade’s chief market strategist JJ Kinahan wrote in a report that “investors might want to be careful late in the session, because it’s in the last hour that things have gotten pretty weird lately.” One could probably bank on a lot of weird hours apart from that in the near future.
